name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3475
preamble: Puzzled? No more cross words! Read Kosman and Picciotto on “Solving The Nation’s Cryptic Puzzles.” Or watch this video.

clue.text: Stand and kick habit, to begin with

indicators.note: what comes to begin with is the opening letter only of the word just before

blocks.note: to kick is to boot
the first letter of habit

explanation.surface: A recovering addict resolving to stand firm and kick the habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kick habit' reads as one phrase about quitting, but kick and habit work separately. Shirley Booth is one of the Oscar-winning actresses in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A booth is a stall at a fair or market, which is also called a stand.

clue.text: Papal decree to authorize eating head of cow or steer

indicators.note: a word that eats something takes it inside itself
the head of a word is its leading letter

blocks.note: a papal bull is a formal edict from the Pope
to OK something is to approve it
the first letter of cow

explanation.surface: The Vatican issuing a ruling on whether beef may be eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papal decree' looks like the definition at the start, but the definition is the last word. Sandra Bullock is one of the theme's Oscar winners.
explanation.definitionFit: A steer is a castrated young bull raised for beef, which is exactly what a bullock is.

clue.text: University taken over by terrible dragon is ready for anything

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters are jumbled out of their order

blocks.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university
taken as written

explanation.surface: A college campus menaced by a fearsome dragon must be prepared for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The university's letter is swallowed into the dragon's letters before they are jumbled together.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on guard is to be alert and prepared for whatever might happen.

clue.text: Pursue barbarian on time

blocks.note: the Huns were barbarian invaders of the Roman world
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Chasing down a barbarian, and doing it punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: Helen Hunt is one of the theme's Oscar-winning actresses.
explanation.definitionFit: To hunt is to chase or seek out, the same as pursue.

clue.text: Arrow maker in Florida — one who leaves an impression?

blocks.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida
an etcher cuts an image into a plate, leaving an impression

explanation.surface: An archery craftsman in Florida who makes a lasting mark on people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who leaves an impression' sounds like a memorable person; the question mark flags the literal sense of someone engraving. Louise Fletcher is a theme Oscar winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A fletcher is a craftsman who makes arrows, the word coming from the old French for arrow.

clue.text: Turn in offensive play!

blocks.note: first meaning: to take to one's bed, as one does on turning in
second meaning: a basketball shot played close to the basket while attacking

explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive play' suggests a rude drama; in American sport, offence is the attacking side. Both phrases define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In basketball a layup is an attacking close-range shot, and to lay up is to retire to bed or rest.

clue.text: Bachelor enters appropriate place to work out — that's one way to create space

indicators.note: a letter that enters a word goes inside it

blocks.note: to appropriate something is to take it
B is the abbreviation for bachelor
the Y is American shorthand for the YMCA, a gym

explanation.surface: A single man joins a gym, which is one way to make room in his life.
explanation.walkthrough: In the US 'the Y' is the everyday name for the YMCA and its gyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing the tab key on a keyboard inserts horizontal blank space, an indent, in text.

clue.text: For the most part, Weinstein and a couple of stars reap what was sown

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is kept, so its final letter goes
a couple means two, so only the opening pair of letters is kept

blocks.note: Harvey Weinstein, the disgraced film producer
the first two letters of stars

explanation.surface: A comment that the disgraced producer and his famous accusers are getting what they deserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at karma for Weinstein, but the last four words are a plain definition of gathering crops.
explanation.definitionFit: To harvest is to gather in a crop that was planted earlier.

clue.text: Savage raid engulfing Yemen's capital, starting from hostile Saudi city

indicators.note: a capital letter is the one at the front of a word
what a word starts from is its first letter
something savaged is mauled out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
to engulf is to swallow something up inside

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Yemen
the first letter of hostile

explanation.surface: A brutal cross-border attack on Yemen launched from a Saudi city.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a war report, and the Saudi capital is in the story as well as being the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: John Roberts originally upholds all but the first piece of oath during economic upswing

indicators.text: all but the first piece of
indicators.note: everything except the opening letter is kept, so that letter is dropped
the original part of a word is where it begins, its first letter
in a down light, what holds something up sits beneath it, so this piece comes after
something happening during a period sits inside it

blocks.note: oath without its first letter
the first letter of Roberts
a boom is a period of rapid economic growth

explanation.surface: Chief Justice John Roberts upholding an oath of office during a period of prosperity.
explanation.walkthrough: John Roberts is the US Chief Justice, so 'John' looks like part of his name; on its own it is American slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang the john is the toilet, so a bathroom in the euphemistic sense.

clue.text: Famous LSD advocate embraces grand goal…

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms around, so one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: Timothy Leary, the 1960s psychologist who promoted LSD
G is slang for a grand, a thousand dollars
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: The well-known psychedelic guru taking on an ambitious mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous' seems to describe the advocate, but it is the definition; the advocate is Timothy Leary.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendary means so celebrated as to be the stuff of legend, that is, very famous.

clue.text: …by swallowing stray fruit

indicators.note: a word that swallows something takes it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: reaching the goal by eating some stray fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots tie the surface to the clue before, but the wordplay stands alone. Halle Berry is a theme Oscar winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A berry is a small juicy fruit such as a strawberry or blueberry.

clue.text: Like some exams after commencement, displaying a sense of right and wrong

indicators.note: what is left after the commencement is the word once its start is gone

blocks.clueFragment: a sense of right and wrong
blocks.note: moral means concerned with right and wrong

explanation.surface: Tests taken after graduation that check a student's ethics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commencement' suggests a graduation ceremony, as Americans call it; here it is just the start of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral exam is one taken by speaking rather than writing.

clue.text: Send small joint

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Mailing off a little marijuana cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a cannabis cigarette; it is the body's joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To ship goods is to send them by carrier.

clue.text: Castro redeploying district leader to the east for agricultural area

indicators.text: redeploying district leader to the east
indicators.note: the leading letter of district is redeployed, moved over to the eastern, right-hand end

blocks.note: Fidel Castro, the Cuban leader

explanation.surface: Cuba's leader reassigning a regional official eastward to farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'District leader' is the first letter of district, D, and 'to the east' sends it to the right-hand end in an across light. Sally Field is a theme Oscar winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A field is an enclosed piece of farmland used for crops or grazing.

clue.text: Regrets offer to hold back support

indicators.note: the words hold the letters, and back says they are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Politely declining an offer to restrain one's backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regrets' sounds like a polite refusal of the offer; the two words simply contain the letters, backwards. Jodie Foster is a theme Oscar winner.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster is to encourage or nurture, so to support something's growth.

clue.text: Senior, for example, or contrarian acknowledges receipt

indicators.note: a contrarian goes the opposite way, so the preceding words run backwards

blocks.note: Sr. is the abbreviation for senior
e.g. stands for for example
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly or awkward customer signing for a delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger is radio slang for 'message received'. Ginger Rogers is one of the theme's Oscar winners.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio procedure 'Roger' confirms a message was received, so to roger is to confirm receiving it.

clue.text: Lunatic did in knockout youngster

indicators.note: something lunatic is crazy and disordered, so the letters are scrambled
one part is placed in the other

blocks.note: taken as written
KO is the abbreviation for a boxing knockout

explanation.surface: A madman knocked out a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiddo is a familiar term for a child or young person.

clue.text: River running west and east at location in reverse

indicators.note: west is leftward, so in an across light the word is written right to left

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river, written here flowing westward
the same river again, now flowing east, so it reads normally
a site is a location

explanation.surface: A river that flows both ways at a spot where it turns back on itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and east' has the river written a second time in its normal direction, so it appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of something is its reverse, the thing contrary to it.

clue.text: About 11, quietly wear away chemical compound

indicators.note: a word that goes about something surrounds it

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to erode is to wear away
XI is 11 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A chemical compound that slowly eats away at something.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is simply the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Peroxide, such as hydrogen peroxide, is a compound containing two linked oxygen atoms.

clue.text: Second alternative to milk for a loud baby, perhaps?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a creamer is a non-dairy whitener added to coffee instead of milk

explanation.surface: Choosing a backup to milk for a noisy infant.
explanation.walkthrough: The milk-and-baby scene points to feeding, but the baby is the definition, with 'perhaps' marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A screamer is someone who screams, and a loud baby is one example.

clue.text: Beginning to chase us around, sailor raised sword

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
in a down light, raising a word turns it upside down so it reads backwards
one word goes around the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: the first letter of chase
taken as written
an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A pirate starting to chase us, holding his sword aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short, curved sword once carried by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Moving front to back, drain jugs

indicators.note: the leading letter is taken off the start and put on the end

blocks.note: a sewer is a drain for waste water

explanation.surface: Shifting position to tip out the pitchers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewers are large wide-mouthed pitchers, formerly used for carrying washing water.

clue.text: Flexible source of characters in Ecclesiastes

indicators.note: the source of characters is the stock of different letters a word draws on, each counted once, so repeats are dropped
doubling as the definition, flexible says those letters bend into a new order

blocks.note: the book of the Old Testament, taken as written

explanation.surface: A pliable origin for the figures in a book of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecclesiastes uses only seven different letters, E, C, L, S, I, A and T, and those seven, rearranged, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic means able to stretch and spring back, so flexible.

clue.text: Person tending to lamb (rare, not well-done) supervised by that woman

indicators.note: something not done well is botched, so its letters come out in a muddle
in a down light, what is supervised sits beneath its overseer, so it comes second

blocks.note: she refers to that woman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook overseen by a woman, warned not to overcook the lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare, not well-done' reads as a steak order, but 'not well-done' signals the jumble. Norma Shearer is a theme Oscar winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A shearer clips the wool from sheep, so tends to lambs and their fleece.

clue.text: One who takes too much public transportation in chaotic era

indicators.note: something chaotic is in disorder, so these letters are shuffled
one part is set inside the other

blocks.note: a bus is a form of public transport
taken as written

explanation.surface: A greedy commuter riding too much transit in turbulent times.
explanation.definitionFit: An abuser is someone who overuses a substance, taking more than is safe.

clue.text: Moderates try to return, imbued with energy

indicators.note: a word that returns goes back the way it came, so it is read backwards
to be imbued with something is to have it inside you

blocks.note: to have a stab at something is to try it
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Political centrists trying to make an energetic comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderates' reads as political centrists, but it is a verb; to bate is to restrain, as in 'with bated breath'. Kathy Bates is a theme Oscar winner.
explanation.definitionFit: To bate is to lessen or restrain something, the root of abate, so it moderates it.

clue.text: Looking at just the rear ends makes the Bayeux Tapestry erotic

indicators.text: Looking at just the rear ends
indicators.note: only the end of each word is kept, its closing letter

blocks.note: the final letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: Studying nothing but the backsides in the medieval embroidery turns it racy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bayeux Tapestry is the eleventh-century embroidery of the Norman conquest of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexy and erotic both describe something sexually arousing.

clue.text: Rock or punk notes

indicators.note: punk means worthless or poor, so the letters are knocked into a different shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Musical notes from rock or punk songs.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock and punk look like a pair of music genres; rock is the definition. Emma Stone is a theme Oscar winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone is a piece of rock, and rock and stone are synonyms for the hard mineral material.

clue.text: Pressure to get old part of a book

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Pressure is making an old part of a book wear out.
explanation.walkthrough: Geraldine Page is a theme Oscar winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is one of the sheets of paper bound into a book.

clue.text: Firm adopting American disguise

indicators.note: to adopt something is to take it in, so one part goes inside

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
Am. is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A company taking on an American cover identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Camo is short for camouflage, a pattern or covering that conceals.

clue.text: Elegant bird with duck's tail

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a swan is a large water bird
the last letter of duck

explanation.surface: A graceful waterbird alongside a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: Swank is chiefly American for stylish, like swanky. Hilary Swank is a theme Oscar winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Swank, as an adjective, means stylish and luxurious, the same as swanky.

clue.text: See 6
Painting is almost red after some alterations

indicators.note: the letters have been altered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter of both words

explanation.surface: A canvas that has been retouched until it is nearly red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' looks like an instruction to cut a letter from red, but both words are taken whole as the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a painting by a great European artist from before about 1800.

clue.text: Changes the arrangement of vacation, for sure, to include a bit of leisure

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in, inside the other part
only a small piece is kept, its opening letter

blocks.note: a rest is a break, like a vacation
yes is an affirmation, as in for sure
the first letter of leisure

explanation.surface: Reworking holiday plans to make sure there is some downtime.
explanation.definitionFit: To restyle is to redesign or rearrange something, such as hair or a layout.

clue.text: Ring to mark award won by 13 actresses in the completed grid

definitions.text: award won by 13 actresses in the completed grid

blocks.note: O is shaped like a ring
a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: Engraving a ring to commemorate a prize won by actresses.
explanation.walkthrough: The thirteen winners are BOOTH, FLETCHER, BERRY, FIELD, BATES, PAGE, SWANK, HUNT, BULLOCK, ROGERS, SHEARER, STONE and FOSTER, all Best Actress Oscar winners.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar is the Academy Award statuette, given for Best Actress among other categories.
